clue.text: Vilified family goes into action

indicators.note: one thing going into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: an action is a deed
FAM is a short informal form of family

explanation.surface: A whole household is slandered as it springs into action.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean spoken ill of, having one's reputation attacked.

clue.text: Show pleasure when Rex falls into the trap

indicators.note: something falling into a trap ends up inside it

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone smiles as the king tumbles into a snare set for him.
explanation.walkthrough: A GIN is an old word for an animal trap; R (Rex, king, as in royal signatures) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smile is the face's display of happiness, a verb phrase matching the verb.

clue.text: Self-contained friend upset by monstrous female

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for self-contained, as in flat adverts

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A self-sufficient person's friend is distressed by a frightful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALLY to YLLA. SC for self-contained is a British estate-agent abbreviation for a flat with its own facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this sea-monster with six heads guarded the strait opposite Charybdis.

clue.text: Dispatched about ten cents for deposit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: dispatched means sent
a dime is a US coin worth ten cents

explanation.surface: Someone posted around ten cents to pay a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' looks like a payment, but here it is silt settling at the bottom of a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt or matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid is a geological deposit.

clue.text: Dashing young chaps take wine when hunting

parts.note: a blood is an old word for a fashionable, spirited young man
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Fashionable young men drink wine while out with the hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOODS is old-fashioned British slang for dashing young men about town.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox hunting is a classic field activity where animals are killed for entertainment.

clue.text: Infuriated when grenade exploded

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone was enraged when a bomb went off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean made furious, past-tense verbs of rage.

clue.text: Poet, a country bumpkin full of sin

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it inside, so one word contains the other

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated rural person
to err is to sin or go astray

explanation.surface: A rustic poet is described as a sinful yokel.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Herrick was a seventeenth-century English lyric writer, author of 'Gather ye rosebuds'.

clue.text: Refuse to settle down

definitions.meaning: to refuse an offer is to turn it down
to sink or go down, as a sun or a price falls

explanation.surface: Someone will not agree to put down roots.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both turning down an invitation and sinking or falling.

clue.text: Agree to attend college?

definitions.meaning: to reach agreement or accept a situation
academic sessions are called terms, so arriving for them is attending college

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: 'terms' as university sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reach an agreement or accept something; literally it is arriving for the academic sessions.

clue.text: Made Colin and Anne consume many a pasta dish

indicators.note: to consume is to take inside, so the rearranged names hold the extra letter
made in the sense of made up or fashioned, so the names are refashioned

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Two people are forced to eat lots of a pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' is a crossword convention for a Roman numeral; here L, fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Large tubes of pasta, stuffed and baked, served as an Italian meal.

clue.text: Warning for old people

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: A caution is given to the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign foretelling something, usually bad.

clue.text: Reminder to lay down rice wine

parts.note: to lay down wine is to keep it in store to mature
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone stores a Japanese rice wine for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay down' is cellar language for storing wine to age.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento kept to recall a person or event.

clue.text: Genuflect during prayer used by cleric

indicators.note: one action happening during another sits inside it, so one word holds the other
used in the sense of worn or knocked about, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: to genuflect is to bend the knee

explanation.surface: A churchman kneels during worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a loose signal for rearrangement, as in worn or knocked about; a prebendary is a cathedral canon.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon who receives a stipend from a cathedral is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: English flower festival

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A celebration of English blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian spring feast celebrating the Resurrection.

clue.text: Fabulous beauty treatment only for thee

indicators.note: treatment in the sense of handling or processing, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A beauty salon promises a special treatment just for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges ONLY FOR THEE. 'Fabulous' means legendary, not merely wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend she was the most beautiful woman, whose abduction caused the Trojan War.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: to charm is to delight or enchant
a door or gate by which one enters

explanation.surface: Someone's charm wins their admission.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: en-TRANCE and EN-trance.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enchant; as a noun, a door or gateway one enters by.

clue.text: Noble knight cheated after festival

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the answer

parts.note: a gala is a festival or celebration
to be had is to be cheated or fooled

explanation.surface: An honourable knight was swindled following a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheated' gives HAD as in 'I've been had'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad was the purest knight of the Round Table, finder of the Holy Grail.

clue.text: Energetic socialite returned in torment

indicators.note: returned in the sense of sent back, so the run of both words is read backwards

parts.note: live means lively or energetic, as in a live wire
a deb, short for debutante, is a young society woman

explanation.surface: A lively young society woman comes back in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LIVEDEB backwards, giving BED + EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague or harass someone persistently, a verb of tormenting.

clue.text: The Spanish exam is most up to date

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in Spanish
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A Spanish exam is described as the newest.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest or most recent, a superlative.

clue.text: Sour beer added to mutton

indicators.note: added to places the second piece after the first

parts.note: in printing an em is called a mutton, to tell it apart from an en (nut)
bitter is a British style of beer

explanation.surface: Bitter ale is drunk alongside a meal of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a hoppy British draught beer; 'mutton' is printers' slang for an em space.
explanation.definitionFit: To sour someone is to make them resentful, a verb.

clue.text: Forbidden for a retired woman

annotationWithheld.why: Forbidden for a retired woman (6): the parse is ANN in BED, with 'retired' giving BED and also signalling the containment, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Fat, heartless Caledonian grandee

indicators.note: heartless means losing the heart, so the central letter of the word goes

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner; Caledonian means Scottish

explanation.surface: An overweight, cruel Scottish landowner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like a description of the grandee but removes the central I of LAIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Nowadays a churchman has to exercise control

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era, so it stands for nowadays
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Today a clergyman must take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or run affairs is to govern them, a verb phrase.

clue.text: Small animal shelter in the Channel Islands

parts.note: Noah's ark sheltered animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A tiny refuge for animals on a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'one found among the Channel Islands', the group of British islands off France.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car-free island near Guernsey belongs to that archipelago.

clue.text: Criticise local wine-storage facility

parts.note: a local is a British pub, a bar
bottles are stored in a wine rack

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the pub's wine cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British for one's nearby pub. To barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle or jeer loudly at a performer is to attack them verbally.

clue.text: To an umpire wet weather is a burden

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an umpire
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: An umpire finds a downpour a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' is not a load here but the old word for a song's repeated chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus repeated in a song, an old musical sense of the word.
